correctness.rationale: All 6907 identity-containing divisor-sized candidate sets are checked exhaustively. A disjoint-cover recursion enumerates every identity-containing complement, while exact Gaussian-integer character sums and finite clique/subgroup tests prove existence of a common spectrum and failure of subgroup-coset spectra for exactly 460 of the 715 normalized tiles. A separate direct-complement implementation verifies explicit universal witnesses and subgroup enumeration for all 19 affine classes and checks their exact coverage of the same 715 normalized tiles. Translation-stabilizer counting yields 2155 total tiles, of which 1168 have no subgroup-coset universal spectrum. Both standalone programs were executed from their actual included paths; outputs are embedded in verify_output.txt. All quantifiers range only over finite subsets of (Z/4Z)^2; no generalization is inferred.

originality.rationale: The nearest public group-specific census proves the tiling/spectral equivalence and its 2155/19 baseline, but makes no universal simultaneous-complement assertion and no subgroup-obstruction classification. Lagarias-Wang, Farkas-Matolcsi-Mora, Zhou, and Kolountzakis-Matolcsi provide definitions, global equivalences, partial special cases, or counterexamples on other groups, not the exact 1168 obstruction count. Results were compared by logical implication, including the distinction between separate spectra and a single common spectrum. Unindexed equivalent classifications remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: A preexisting unindexed article or unpublished certificate may independently tabulate non-subgroup universal spectra for this finite group.

An implicit noncyclic stronger consequence from older factorization literature may exist beyond the material inspected; the published small-group spectral census alone does not establish the 1168 obstruction count.
Independent external mathematical verification has not been performed.

value.rationale: Universal complement spectra require one Fourier basis for every complement, a mathematically motivated robustness notion in tiling Fourier analysis. The exact 1168/2155 obstruction demonstrates that more than half of the tiles in a canonical rank-two exponent-four group cannot use subgroup-character bases although a universal basis exists. The complete 19-orbit witnesses classify the precise geometry needed for non-subgroup designs, provide a reusable exact small-group boundary test for methods based on annihilator subgroups, and are not a random parameter slice. The known 2155 individual tile/spectrum count is treated as baseline rather than the claimed novelty.
